blocks.text: Token validators use JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) signed by your identity provider (IdP) to enforce authentication requirements.
Your IdP's JWT must contain the following claims when configuring a token validator:

blocks.item: Subject (sub): Identifies the principal that is the subject of the JWT. This claim represents the user or entity making the request.
Audience (aud): Specifies the intended recipients of the JWT.
Issuer (iss): Identifies the issuer of the JWT.

blocks.text: You can add more claims depending on your IdP's JWT.
You can use jwt.io to inspect and extract the required preceding information from a JWT issued by your app’s IdP.
To access the Token Validator page, go to Authentication > User Authentication > Token Validator.
On the Token Validator page, you can:

blocks.item: Add a token validator.
On the Token Validator page, click Add Token Validator.
The Add Token Validator drawer appears.
In the Add Token Validator drawer:
Name: Enter the name of the token validator.
Access Type: Select Mobile Apps or Browser Access to determine which apps you want to add a token validator for.
If you select Browser Access, the app must have Browser Access enabled.
Target Applications: Select the name of the app key you previously registered.
JWT Claim Validation: Enter the following information from the JWT issued by your app's IdP:
exp: This field displays to show the field is enforced. You cannot configure this field.
sub: This field displays to show the field is enforced. You cannot configure this field.
iat: This field displays to show the field is enforced. You cannot configure this field.
aud: Enter the Value listed from the JWT's aud. You cannot configure the Name.
iss: Enter the Value listed from the JWT's iss. You cannot configure the Name.
Click Add Claim to enter more values as required.
Depending on your app's IdP or if Browser Access is enabled, the values might differ.
Signature Validation: Select a Validation Type and depending on what you selected:
Client JWKS URL: Enter your JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) URL from your app's IdP.
Certificates and Public Keys: Upload the certificate used by your app's IdP to sign JWTs.
See image.
Click Save.
Update a token validator.
On the Token Validator page, click the Edit icon on the token validator.
The Update Token Validator drawer appears.
In the Update Token Validator drawer:
Name: Edit the name of the token validator.
Target Applications: Select the name of your registered app.
JWT Claim Validation: Edit any of the claim requirements and their values or click Add Claim to create more claim requirements.
Depending on what you selected as a Validation Type:
Client JWKS URL: Edit the JWKS URL.
Certificates and Public Keys: Upload a new certificate or public key used by your app's IdP to sign JWTs.
See image.
Click Save.
Delete a token validator.
On the Token Validator page, click the Delete icon on the token validator.
The Delete Token Validator window appears.
In the Delete Token Validator window, click Delete to confirm deletion of the token validator.
See image.
On the Token Validator page, a confirmation window briefly appears.

blocks.heading: Public Key Format of Token Validator

blocks.text: After you have added the token validator and if you want to configure it to verify JWTs, you can opt to supply the public key in PEM format.
The general guidelines for the public key in PEM format are:

blocks.item: Contains the standard BEGIN and END PUBLIC KEY PEM headers
Follows the standard Rivest–Shamir–Adleman (RSA) algorithm for a PEM format
